directoryStems.mcq-4c5e3d0b0dc72c3a12baa7a7: בן 82, דייר בבית אבות, מובא להערכה בעקבות אירועים חוזרים של "כמעט" איבוד הכרה. האירועים מתרחשים בדרך כלל כשעה לאחר הארוחות, ולעיתים מלוות בתחושת סחרחורת וחולשה. בהיסטוריה הרפואית: יתר לחץ דם, סוכרת סוג 2 ומחלת פרקינסון. בבדיקה גופנית בשכיבה – לחץ דם142/82מ"מ כספית, דופק 68 לדקה. מדידת לחץ דם שבוצעה 90 דקות לאחר ארוחת צהריים הדגימה לחץ דם סיסטולי של 118 מ"מ כספית. מהו המנגנון הפיזיולוגי העיקרי התורם לירידה בלחץ הדם לאחר הארוחה במטופל זה?

highlightAliases.old: Episodic dizziness timing clue: <1 minute suggests BPPV; 20 to 120 minutes suggests TIA or migraine; >120 minutes to 2 days suggests Meniere disease/recurrent vestibulopathy (p670)
highlightAliases.new: Episode duration is a clue. BPPV typically causes positional attacks lasting less than 1 minute. Spontaneous attacks can overlap in TIA, vestibular migraine and Ménière disease. Definite Ménière disease includes attacks lasting 20 minutes–12 hours with characteristic auditory findings; probable episodes can last up to 24 hours (p670; Bárány Society criteria).

highlightAliases.old: ICD indicated for syncope + VT with EF <35%, syncope + prior MI, or VT induced on electrophysiologic study (p675)
highlightAliases.new: Syncope caused by sustained VT warrants electrophysiologic assessment for an ICD, including ventricular function and reversible causes. After a previous MI, unexplained syncope with inducible sustained VT on electrophysiologic study is an ICD indication. Previous MI alone does not justify implantation (p675; ESC syncope guideline).

highlightAliases.old: Drug doses for severe OH/PPH: caffeine 250 mg (2 cups brewed) each morning, fludrocortisone 0.1–0.5 mg po daily, midodrine 2.5–10 mg po TID, octreotide 50 mg subQ 30 min pre-meal (unusually high vs. the mcg doses typically used clinically — this is the book's own printed text) (p675)Current practice (not the book): the source trial gave octreotide 50 micrograms (µg) subQ, not 50 mg — Jansen et al., 1989 (PubMed 2646315).
highlightAliases.new: For severe symptomatic OH, specialist options include midodrine 2.5–10 mg up to three times daily while awake (avoid near bedtime) or fludrocortisone 0.05–0.2 mg daily with potassium, edema and supine BP monitoring. Avoid fludrocortisone in heart failure. For postprandial hypotension, the chapter discusses caffeine 250 mg in the morning and a small study of subcutaneous octreotide 50 micrograms before a glucose load (p675; OH review, AHA statement).Octreotide was studied in micrograms. The textbook’s milligram unit overstates the trial dose by a factor of 1,000 (Jansen et al., 1989).

highlightAliases.old: Episodes lasting <1 minute suggest BPPV; 20 to 120 minutes suggest TIA or migraine; more than 120 minutes up to 2 days suggest Meniere disease or recurrent vestibulopathy (p670).
highlightAliases.new: BPPV commonly causes positional spells under 1 minute. TIA and vestibular migraine can overlap in duration. Definite Ménière attacks last 20 minutes–12 hours with characteristic auditory findings, and probable attacks can last up to 24 hours (p670; Bárány Society criteria, PMID 25882471).

highlightAliases.old: OH-contributing drug classes: antipsychotics (MAOIs, TCAs), diuretics, beta-blockers, nitrates/alpha-blockers — alpha+beta combination especially dangerous (p668)
highlightAliases.new: Drugs that can contribute to OH include antipsychotics, antidepressants such as MAOIs and TCAs, diuretics, beta-blockers, nitrates and alpha-blockers. Combined alpha and beta blockade further impairs compensation on standing (p668)

highlightAliases.old: CSS = CSH plus syncope on stimulation; vasovagal syncope or OH coexists in one-third of CSH patients; about half of CSS patients sustain an injury/fracture during episodes (p669)
highlightAliases.new: CSS requires an abnormal response that reproduces the patient’s usual spontaneous symptoms in a compatible clinical history; vasovagal syncope or OH coexists in one-third of CSH patients; about half of CSS patients sustain an injury/fracture during episodes (p669)

highlightAliases.old: Seizures may occur during a syncopal event as a consequence of cerebral hypoperfusion, but are rarely a cause of syncope (p665).
highlightAliases.new: Brief myoclonic jerks can occur during syncope from hypoperfusion. They do not, by themselves, establish an epileptic seizure (p665).

highlightAliases.old: What is the diagnostic yield of a 24-hour ambulatory Holter monitor in an unselected syncope population, and what device is replacing it?
highlightAliases.new: What is the diagnostic yield of a 24-hour ambulatory Holter monitor in an unselected syncope population, and when can longer monitoring help?

highlightAliases.old: Only 1% to 2% diagnostic yield in unselected populations; implantable loop recorders (ILRs), with higher diagnostic yield, are increasingly recommended as an early diagnostic tool, especially in older patients (p671–672).
highlightAliases.new: Only 1% to 2% diagnostic yield in unselected populations; a Holter is useful when symptoms are frequent. An implantable loop recorder can capture an infrequent recurrent episode when arrhythmia remains a concern after the initial assessment (p671–672).

highlightAliases.old: For OH or postprandial hypotension, p675 lists morning caffeine 250 mg, oral fludrocortisone 0.1–0.5 mg daily, oral midodrine 2.5–10 mg three times daily, and subcutaneous octreotide 30 minutes before a meal. The printed octreotide dose is 50 mg [sic — the cited study used 50 micrograms, not milligrams]. Jansen et al., 1989.
